title: Big eruptions cool the planet for years
body: Tambora's 1815 eruption injected sulphur into the stratosphere, where sulfate aerosols spread globally, dimming sunlight enough that 1816 became the Year Without a Summer, with crop failures across continents. Stratospheric aerosols ignore rain, lasting years, unlike low ash that washes out in weeks. Climate has a volcanic dimmer switch with a long memory.
